seoTitle: How is a piano move carried out?
seoDesc: Need to move a piano? Trust removal professionals for safe transport.
h1: Piano removals: precautions, methods and advice

intro.p: The piano is an instrument as majestic as it is delicate. Upright or grand, moving one is a real challenge, both technically and logistically. Weight, fragility, sentimental or financial value: many factors make this type of transport particularly difficult. In this article, discover some practical advice and precautions for moving your piano.

sections.h: Why is moving a piano so special?

body.p: A piano is not a piece of furniture like any other. It is a precision instrument made up of thousands of parts, some of which are extremely sensitive to knocks, vibrations or changes in temperature. It must therefore be handled with the greatest care.

An upright piano can weigh between 150 and 300 kg, and a grand piano can exceed 500 kg. Their bulky shape makes them hard to grip, and moving them can quickly become dangerous without suitable equipment.
Despite their apparent sturdiness, pianos are very sensitive to jolts. The slightest knock can put the instrument out of tune, damage the mechanism or harm the wooden structure.
Beyond its purchase price, a piano can have sentimental or artistic value. Some antique or high-end models deserve particular attention during transport.

sections.h: The key stages of a successful piano move

body.p: Moving a piano cannot be improvised. It is essential to plan each stage carefully so the transport is safe.

Before any handling, the premises must be inspected: door widths, stairs, lift, floor covering and so on. This assessment determines whether some parts will need to be dismantled or whether a furniture lift is required.

sections.h: Types of piano and their particularities

body.p: Not all pianos are transported in the same way. Methods vary according to their shape and weight.

sections.h: The risks of an unsupervised move

body.p: Trying to move a piano yourself may seem tempting to save money. Yet the consequences can be serious:

ul: Breakage or damage to the piano
Damage to the property (walls, stairs, floors)
Unexpected costs for repairs or retuning

body.p: It is often not worth the risk.

As you can see, moving a piano takes know-how, precision and specific equipment. By entrusting this task to a company specialising in piano removals, you know your instrument is in good hands. Whether you are a private individual or a professional, don't leave your piano's fate to chance: call on the experts.
